correctness.rationale: For the rooted star, the source's cover-difference coordinates reduce every proper tube to a nonempty proper leaf subset, with total sum fixed at \(n^{2n}\). The affine metric is exactly the standard metric in those difference coordinates because the root coordinate is constant. Singleton facets give a global upper bound and force the uniform leaf-difference center at equality. For a subset of size \(k\), the exact projected-normal norm and slack give the displayed distance \(D_k\); the proof shows \(D_k>D_1\) for every \(k\ge2\). Thus the candidate ball is feasible, optimal, uniquely centered, and tangent exactly to singleton-tube facets.

value.rationale: Poset associahedra are a recent family extending several classical associahedral constructions, and Sack's realization was designed to make their compactification geometry explicit. The rooted-star specialization is the natural maximally symmetric branching test case: combinatorially permutohedral, yet metrically governed by the source's rapidly varying tube scales. The theorem gives a complete exact metric answer for the whole family and shows that only \(n-1\) smallest tubes among \(2^{n-1}-2\) facets control the inball. This isolates a concrete geometric effect of the realization rather than merely recomputing a classical permutohedron radius.
